title: WITHDRAWN (MISREAD) — Account and Address: clearing Contact Phone 1 leaves the Save button fully enabled but clicking it issues no save (the field does turn red) — same wiring as BUG-LOC-LI-001
requirementSource: Location Settings -> Account and Address sub-tab (/navigator/locations/<office>/settings/location). Contact Phone 1 is a populated, editable, validity-checked field — the application itself sets aria-invalid="true" when it is emptied, so the application treats the empty value as invalid. Archetype ARCH-001 'save-enabled-on-invalid-form-no-feedback' in specs_planning/_internal/bug-archetypes.md defines this as a file-on-reproduction defect and already names a colleague flag on this same class of field (TC-LOS-BAS-016, 'Phone 1 accepts non-phone text, save stays enabled'). Encore field-case rule specs_planning/_internal/field-case-generation.md §2.1 requires every rejected value to be BOTH announced and escapable.
stepsToReproduce: Confirm the starting state: Contact Phone 1 (data-testid=location-settings-input-contact-phone-1) reads '202.216.0113' and the Save button is disabled.
Click into Contact Phone 1, select all its text, and press Delete so the field is empty.
Press Tab to blur the field naturally.
Observe the field now carries aria-invalid="true" — the form has judged the empty value invalid.
Observe the Save button is now ENABLED despite the form holding a field it has itself marked invalid.
Observe that nothing happens: no 'Save Changes' confirmation dialog appears, no network request is issued, and no error text or toast is shown. The Save button stays enabled.
expectedBehavior: With a field flagged aria-invalid, the Save button must be disabled so the user cannot submit — which is how the legacy Navigator site behaves for the equivalent invalid-form case. If the application instead leaves Save enabled, clicking it must produce a visible rejection signal naming the offending field. Doing neither leaves the user clicking a live button that silently refuses to act.
actualBehavior: WITHDRAWN. Clearing Contact Phone 1 is correctly announced by the application: the label turns red, the input takes a red border, and a red alert icon appears whose tooltip reads 'Required'. The user is told what is wrong and which field is at fault. The Save button does render as enabled while the form is invalid and clicking it issues no request, but since the validation message is already on screen at that point, this is a cosmetic inconsistency rather than a defect. Nothing is persisted and a reload restores the original value.

mcpEvidence.findings: Found by a mandated ARCH-001 pattern sweep across the Location Settings sibling sub-tabs (account-and-address, legal, notes, currency, business-types) after the same symptom was confirmed on Local Information as BUG-LOC-LI-001. Live authenticated Playwright walk (headless, .auth/encore-state.json) against office 1606. The sweep selected the first populated, enabled, visible text input on each active sub-tab panel, cleared it and blurred. On Account and Address that field was location-settings-input-contact-phone-1 with original value '202.216.0113'. Result after clear + Tab: aria-invalid='true', Save button disabled=false. Clicking Save produced dialog='(none)' and a captured network count of 0 across all non-GET /api/ traffic — recorded as MATCHES_ARCH001=true. No save was committed and the page was never reloaded into a mutated state, so office 1606 required no restoration. The other four sub-tabs were skipped by the sweep because no populated editable plain-text input was present on their panels — they are NOT cleared of this defect, merely untested by this probe (see the report's 'Areas NOT tested' note).

baselineEvidence: The legacy Navigator site (navigator2.training.psav.com) was reached and authenticated during this session via shared SSO, but Contact Phone 1 on the Account and Address surface was not observed there: the legacy location list does not carry office 1606 (per LR-ENC-001 the legacy baseline entity is office 1604) and no mutation was attempted on the shared legacy office. The closely-related artifact specs_planning/_internal/old-site-baseline/OSB-ACCESS-VERIFY-2026-04-24.md § 'BUG-LI-001' records that for the Oracle Product field the old site keeps Save DISABLED on an invalid form while the new site enables it, and states 'the Save button is NOT wired to form validity ... a clear regression in the save-button-wiring'. That finding is about the same underlying wiring and strongly suggests this instance is also a regression — but it was observed on a different field and a different sub-tab, so extending it here would be inference rather than observation, and this field is therefore classified not-checked. FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED: walk the legacy site's Account and Address screen for office 1604, clear Contact Phone 1, read the Save button's disabled flag, and reclassify to regression-from-baseline or intentional-UX-change. BASELINE ATTEMPTED 2026-09-21: legacy office 1604 was opened at #/setup/locationdetail/1604 and swept for any input whose id or name matches /phone/i — the sweep returned an EMPTY list, and the page additionally reported 'CRM Account retrieval failed'. The legacy equivalent of the Contact Phone 1 field is therefore not on that screen, and this field could not be compared. baselineComparison stays not-checked. FOLLOW-UP: locate the legacy Account/Address surface (it is not part of the location detail screen) and read the Save button's disabled flag with Contact Phone 1 cleared.
networkEvidence: A page-level request listener capturing every non-GET request to any /api/ URL recorded ZERO requests across the Save click plus a 2 second settle window. Per LR-033 this is the definitive client-blocked signature — the application's own validation refuses to submit but does so silently, neither disabling the button nor rendering an error. Note this is a DIFFERENT symptom from the two Account and Address bugs already on file: BUG-LOC-ACC-001 (Phone 2 cleared) is a save that DOES fire and reports success but fails to persist, and BUG-LOC-ACC-002 is a backend account-search returning empty data. Here the save never reaches the network at all.

verificationLog.verifierAgent: Automated QA (Claude Opus 5) — LR-044 re-verification with visual evidence
verificationLog.verdict: CONFIRMED but DOWNGRADED high -> low; original actualBehavior was overstated
verificationLog.evidence: Re-ran with screenshots and computed styles. The original filing said 'no inline error, no toast'. The field DOES render a visible red border, and a toast was present on screen, so both halves of that claim were wrong. What survives is the same narrow point as BUG-LOC-LI-001: the Save button presents as enabled on an invalid form and no save request is issued when it is clicked.

verificationLog.verifierAgent: Automated QA (Claude Opus 5) — LR-044 re-verification prompted by user challenge
verificationLog.evidence: Re-verified 2026-09-22 after the user challenged the finding. The field DOES announce the problem, in words: on blur the label turns red, the input takes a red border, and a red alert icon appears to the right of the input whose tooltip reads verbatim 'Required'. Confirmed by hovering the icon and reading the tooltip node, plus a screenshot of the rendered tooltip. My original filing missed this because the scrape walked element textContent only — a tooltip that mounts on hover is not in the DOM until hovered, and the alert icon carries no text of its own, so both were invisible to that method. The app therefore satisfies the field-case-generation §2.1 oracle in full: the rejected value is ANNOUNCED (red label + red border + icon + 'Required' tooltip) and ESCAPABLE (Tab moves focus away normally). The residual point — that the Save button renders enabled while the form is invalid — is not a defect on its own: the error is already displayed on the field before Save is ever clicked, so the user is not left without information. No data is altered at any point; a reload restores the original value.
